findings.text: Upheld (Q4, dead path, a defect under the rubric). All three META rows define `annotations` (tools.ts:84-96), so `META[name].annotations === undefined ? {} : …` can never take its `{}` side. The fix is to pass `annotations: META[name].annotations` directly, as memory's tools do (src/modules/memory/tools.ts:327).

Lowered to advisory. The reviewer reports this as a defect: the D-9 (part 2) row names `showsPins` and says the other answer changes its body and tests, but `showsPins` no longer exists in src/ or tests/ (checked); the decision is a comment in `forSessionStart` (contribute.ts:192-196). The sentence is stale against the code. Q11's defect is narrower: a rewrite that drops or alters a fact, hedge or scope limit of the old text, removes an unsourced claim, or invents a source. This is a new document's sentence that no longer matches the code, which no defect condition of this rubric names. The architecture reviewer rates the same line advisory. Fix the ADR row, spec.md:50/164 and probes/check-docs.ts:60 together, or extract the one-line function the record names.

Upheld (Q2 and Q6, across the module's declared rule). The base, CLAUDE.md's knowledge paragraph, says `requireSchema` in schema.ts is what 'everything that reads or writes the tables calls'. This item's own neighbours keep that rule through the module's schema state: contribute.ts:230, compact.ts:118 and doctor's checks.ts:734 (checked). `knowledgeStatus` (report.ts:192-212, added in the diff) checks only that the tables exist, then reads `knowledge_entries.status/problem/pinned` and `knowledge_shown` under no version promise. On a store whose knowledge schema is `too-new`, which openDb lets open, `status` either prints figures under a meaning this binary does not know or throws. This is the same class as round one's compact defect. Fix: return null, or a 'newer than this wizardingcode-mem' line, unless `moduleSchemaState(db, KNOWLEDGE_MODULE, KNOWLEDGE_SCHEMA_VERSION) === "current"`, with a test that records module version 8.
